projects.name: Navi Mumbai International Airport
projects.stat: Built on a blasted-flat hill and a diverted river
projects.summary: Mumbai's second airport, built by Adani Airports with CIDCO on marshland at Ulwe. Before a runway could go down, the Ulwe hill was blasted flat, the Ulwe river was diverted and wetlands were filled. Phase 1 handles 20 million passengers a year; the design scales to 90 million.
projects.watch: Watch Ulwe hill disappear (2017–19) and the river channel get pushed around the airfield, then the lotus-shaped terminal fill in.

milestones.t: First test landing, by an IAF C-295

projects.name: Noida International Airport, Jewar
projects.stat: Farmland to a 3.9 km runway in five years
projects.summary: A greenfield airport in Gautam Buddha Nagar, built by YIAPL, a subsidiary of Zurich Airport. Phase 1 has one 3.9 km runway and room for 12 million passengers a year, with later phases planned to make it one of India's largest airports.
projects.watch: Farm plots give way to the runway strip in 2022–23; then the terminal roof, apron and approach roads fill in.

projects.name: Manohar International Airport, Mopa
projects.stat: Goa's second airport, carved into a laterite plateau
projects.summary: A greenfield airport built by GMR on the Mopa plateau in North Goa, taking pressure off the Navy-run Dabolim airport. Phase 1 handles 4.4 million passengers a year.
projects.watch: A bare plateau is levelled into a 3.75 km runway, with the terminal on its southern edge.

projects.name: Kempegowda Airport Terminal 2
projects.stat: A 'terminal in a garden', designed by SOM
projects.summary: Bengaluru airport's second terminal, designed by SOM with indoor forests, hanging gardens and bamboo-clad interiors. It opened to domestic flights in January 2023 and took over international flights later that year.
projects.watch: Construction fields around the old terminal turn into a second terminal, forecourt and multi-level car park.

projects.name: Maharishi Valmiki International Airport, Ayodhya
projects.stat: An airstrip turned international airport in under two years
projects.summary: A small airstrip rebuilt into an international airport to serve pilgrims visiting the Ram Mandir. The terminal's façade draws on Nagara temple architecture.
projects.watch: The short old strip is lengthened, a new apron is laid and the terminal appears in 2023.

projects.name: Rajkot International Airport, Hirasar
projects.stat: Greenfield airport on 1,025 hectares
projects.summary: A greenfield airport about 30 km from Rajkot that replaced the old city-centre airfield in 2023, with a runway long enough for wide-body jets.
projects.watch: Scrubland becomes a runway, taxiways and a terminal between 2019 and 2023.

projects.name: Atal Setu — Mumbai Trans Harbour Link
projects.stat: 21.8 km · India's longest sea bridge
projects.summary: A six-lane bridge across Mumbai harbour from Sewri to Chirle near Nhava Sheva, 16.5 km of it over water. Built by MMRDA with JICA funding, it cut the drive from south Mumbai to Navi Mumbai to about 20 minutes.
projects.watch: Follow the pier line marching out across the mudflats from both shores in 2019–22 until the deck closes.

projects.name: Chenab Rail Bridge
projects.stat: 359 m above the river · world's highest railway arch bridge
projects.summary: A 1,315 m steel arch bridge on the Udhampur–Srinagar–Baramulla rail link, leaping 467 m across the Chenab gorge in Reasi district. Built by Afcons for Konkan Railway to withstand 260 km/h winds, it finally put the Kashmir valley on India's rail network.
projects.watch: The two half-arches creep out from the cliffs and meet in 2021; the deck follows, then trains.

milestones.t: Arch closure — the two halves meet

projects.name: New Pamban Bridge
projects.stat: India's first vertical-lift sea bridge
projects.summary: A 2.07 km railway bridge linking Rameswaram island to the mainland, built by RVNL beside the 1914 Scherzer rolling-lift bridge it replaces. Its 72.5 m navigation span lifts straight up to let ships through.
projects.watch: A new pier line rises alongside the century-old bridge, with the lift-span towers near mid-channel.

projects.name: Sudarshan Setu, Okha–Beyt Dwarka
projects.stat: 2.32 km · India's longest cable-stayed bridge at opening
projects.summary: A four-lane cable-stayed bridge from Okha to Beyt Dwarka island, which until 2024 was reached only by boat. Its 900 m cable-stayed section hangs from two tall pylons in the Gulf of Kutch.
projects.watch: Two pylons rise out of the sea and the deck closes between them around 2023.

projects.name: Bogibeel Bridge
projects.stat: 4.94 km · India's longest rail-cum-road bridge
projects.summary: A double-deck bridge over the Brahmaputra near Dibrugarh, with a road on top and a double-line railway below. Sanctioned in 1997 and started in 2002, it opened in 2018, a vital link to Arunachal Pradesh's frontier.
projects.watch: The last spans are launched across the braided river channels before the 2018 opening.

projects.name: Mumbai Coastal Road
projects.stat: 10.58 km, much of it on land reclaimed from the sea
projects.summary: An expressway from Marine Drive to the Bandra–Worli Sea Link, running on land reclaimed from the Arabian Sea and through twin tunnels under Malabar Hill, India's first undersea road tunnels. The reclamation around Haji Ali is one of the largest in the city's history.
projects.watch: A whole new shoreline of interchanges, sea walls and promenade appears around the Haji Ali shrine from 2019.

milestones.t: Linked to the Bandra–Worli Sea Link

projects.name: Dwarka Expressway
projects.stat: India's first 8-lane elevated urban expressway
projects.summary: A 29 km access-controlled expressway from Shiv Murti near IGI Airport to Kherki Daula in Gurugram, built to take load off NH-48. Most of it runs on a single line of piers, with tunnels linking it to the airport.
projects.watch: A row of piers beside the rail line becomes a wide elevated ribbon with ramps and toll plazas.

milestones.t: Haryana section opened by PM Modi
Delhi section opened by PM Modi

projects.name: Sabarmati Multimodal Hub — Bullet Train Terminus
projects.stat: Terminus of the 508 km Mumbai–Ahmedabad bullet train
projects.summary: India's first high-speed line will run 508 km from Mumbai's BKC to Sabarmati, where this hub ties the bullet-train station to Indian Railways, metro and BRTS. The line uses Japanese Shinkansen technology; all land has been acquired and the first Gujarat section is due around 2027.
projects.watch: The hub building and the elevated high-speed station deck rise over the old railway yard.

milestones.t: Bullet train foundation stone laid in Ahmedabad
All land acquired; over 62% of work done

projects.name: Vizhinjam International Seaport
projects.stat: India's first deep-water container transshipment port
projects.summary: Built by Adani Ports with the Kerala government near Thiruvananthapuram, a few nautical miles from the main East–West shipping lane, with about 20 m of natural depth. Its breakwater was built out into the open sea, and the port now takes the world's largest container ships.
projects.watch: The breakwater curls out into the sea year by year from 2016; container yards and cranes appear by 2024.

milestones.t: Trial operations with the first mother vessel

projects.name: INS Kadamba, Karwar — Project Seabird
projects.stat: Set to become Asia's largest naval base
projects.summary: The Navy's west-coast base at Karwar, built under Project Seabird to move warships and submarines away from crowded Mumbai. Phase IIA adds new piers, a covered dry berth and a naval air station.
projects.watch: New piers and berths extend the harbour, and more hulls appear alongside in recent frames.

projects.name: Mudh–Nyoma Airbase, Ladakh
projects.stat: A fighter-capable runway at ~13,700 ft, ~35 km from the LAC
projects.summary: An old advanced landing ground in eastern Ladakh, rebuilt by the Border Roads Organisation into a fighter-capable airbase with a new 2.7 km runway, one of the highest in the world.
projects.watch: The new paved runway appears beside the old strip on the Indus plain in 2024–25.

milestones.t: Foundation stone laid by the Defence Minister

projects.name: Khavda Renewable Energy Park
projects.stat: Planned 30 GW · the world's largest renewable energy park
projects.summary: A solar-and-wind park on barren salt desert in Kutch, close to the Pakistan border, spread over about 538 km², roughly five times the size of Paris. Adani Green is building most of it, alongside NTPC, GSECL and others, and the first capacity came online in late 2023.
projects.watch: Use the Sentinel-2 yearly layer: from 2022 the desert fills with a grid of panel blocks visible from space.

projects.name: Bhadla Solar Park
projects.stat: 2,245 MW on ~56 km² of the Thar desert
projects.summary: One of the world's largest solar parks, in Jodhpur district, where summer temperatures pass 45°C. It was built in four phases between 2015 and 2020, with developers including Adani, NTPC, ACME and SB Energy.
projects.watch: In the Sentinel-2 years, dark blocks of panels spread across the sand from 2016 to 2019.

projects.name: Pavagada Solar Park (Shakti Sthala)
projects.stat: 2,050 MW on 13,000 acres leased from farmers
projects.summary: Built on drought-hit land in Tumakuru district that farmers lease to the state instead of selling, earning an annual rent. Developed by the Karnataka Solar Power Development Corporation and fully commissioned in 2019.
projects.watch: Compare Sentinel-2 2016 with 2019: scrubland becomes a patchwork of solar blocks.

projects.name: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant
projects.stat: 6 × 1,000 MW VVER reactors when complete
projects.summary: India's largest nuclear station, on the coast near Kanyakumari, built by NPCIL with Russia's Rosatom. Units 1 and 2 have run since 2013 and 2016; units 3 to 6 are being built alongside them, taking the site to 6,000 MW.
projects.watch: New reactor buildings and turbine halls rise beside the two domed units already running.

projects.name: Polavaram Irrigation Project
projects.stat: A national project across the Godavari
projects.summary: A multipurpose dam across the Godavari to irrigate lakhs of hectares, generate 960 MW and send water to the Krishna delta. The spillway was built first; the main rock-fill dam slipped after floods damaged its diaphragm wall in 2020, and the state now targets 2027.
projects.watch: The spillway rises on the bank and cofferdams choke the river channel from 2019.

projects.name: Central Vista & the New Parliament
projects.stat: A triangular Parliament beside the 1927 circular one
projects.summary: The rebuilding of Delhi's power corridor: a new triangular Parliament House next to the old circular one, a redone Kartavya Path (formerly Rajpath), and new Common Central Secretariat buildings replacing post-independence office blocks.
projects.watch: The triangle rises on the plot beside the old Parliament in 2021–22; later frames show ministry blocks being replaced.

projects.name: Statue of Unity
projects.stat: 182 m · the world's tallest statue
projects.summary: A 182-metre statue of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on Sadhu Bet island, just downstream of the Sardar Sarovar dam on the Narmada. Built by L&T around concrete cores clad in bronze panels; a new tourism town, Ekta Nagar, grew up around it.
projects.watch: The earliest frames show a rocky islet; the cores rise by 2017 and a bridge reaches the island.

projects.name: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir, Ayodhya
projects.stat: A three-storey Nagara-style stone temple
projects.summary: A stone temple built by L&T, with Tata Consulting Engineers, for the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra trust. The consecration (Pran Pratishtha) took place in January 2024 and the spire and flag were completed in November 2025.
projects.watch: The site is cleared and excavated in 2020–21, then the temple's plinth and courtyard walls take shape.

milestones.t: Flag hoisted atop the completed shikhara

projects.name: Narendra Modi Stadium, Motera
projects.stat: 1,32,000 seats · world's largest cricket stadium
projects.summary: The old Sardar Patel Stadium at Motera was demolished and rebuilt by L&T as the world's largest cricket stadium, with a membrane roof and no pillars blocking views. It hosted the 2023 ODI World Cup final.
projects.watch: The old bowl vanishes; a bigger ring with its white roof appears by 2019.

milestones.t: Hosts the ODI World Cup final

projects.name: Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham, Varanasi
projects.stat: A temple-to-Ganga corridor cut through the old city
projects.summary: A pilgrim corridor that cleared a dense knot of old-city lanes to connect the Kashi Vishwanath temple directly to the Ganga ghats. Around 300 properties were acquired, and dozens of old shrines were rediscovered inside demolished houses.
projects.watch: Rooftops vanish in 2019–20 and an open stone plaza runs down to the river.

projects.name: Bharat Mandapam, Pragati Maidan
projects.stat: The G20 Leaders' Summit venue
projects.summary: Pragati Maidan's 1970s exhibition halls, including the brutalist Hall of Nations, were demolished to build a new exhibition-and-convention centre, named Bharat Mandapam. It hosted the G20 Leaders' Summit in September 2023.
projects.watch: The old hall complex gives way to the new convention centre between 2019 and 2023.

projects.name: Yashobhoomi — IICC, Dwarka
projects.stat: One of the world's largest convention & expo venues
projects.summary: The India International Convention & Expo Centre in Dwarka Sector 25, with a main hall seating thousands and vast exhibition halls, linked to the Airport Express metro line.
projects.watch: A bare plot beside the Airport Express line fills with exhibition halls in 2020–23.

projects.name: Shri Mahakal Lok, Ujjain
projects.stat: A 900 m temple corridor along Rudra Sagar lake
projects.summary: A temple corridor around the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga, lined with murals, statues and carved pillars along the edge of Rudra Sagar lake.
projects.watch: The lake's edge is rebuilt into a broad walkway lined with sculptures.

projects.name: GIFT City, Gandhinagar
projects.stat: India's first International Financial Services Centre
projects.summary: Gujarat International Finance Tec-City, a planned financial district on the Sabarmati between Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar. It hosts India's IFSC, with international exchanges, banks and funds, and towers keep rising in its core.
projects.watch: Empty plots around the first twin towers fill with high-rises, 2014–2026.

milestones.t: India INX, the first international exchange, opens
IFSCA, the unified regulator, is set up

projects.name: Amaravati Capital City
projects.stat: A greenfield capital on land pooled from farmers
projects.summary: Andhra Pradesh's planned capital on the Krishna, built on land pooled from tens of thousands of farmers. Roads and buildings went up from 2016, work largely stopped in 2019 under a 'three capitals' plan, and it was revived in 2024 and relaunched in May 2025.
projects.watch: A grid of arterial roads appears in 2016–19, fades under weeds, then comes back to life.

projects.name: Dholera Smart City (SIR)
projects.stat: A 920 km² investment region, home to India's first commercial chip fab
projects.summary: A greenfield industrial city on the flat salt plains between Ahmedabad and Bhavnagar, planned under the Delhi–Mumbai Industrial Corridor. Roads, utilities and the first factories have come up in its activation area, and Tata Electronics is building a ₹91,000 crore semiconductor fab in the region.
projects.watch: Blank salt pans turn into a grid of roads, drains and industrial sheds.

milestones.t: Foundation stone for Tata's semiconductor fab
